Subject: DPA + SCCs / UK IDTA questions before legal review

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the product looked promising. Our procurement team is kicking off the legal review and asked for a couple of things before we hand to counsel: 1) the latest DPA with your redlines (any version that already references SCCs or UK IDTA is great), 2) a current subprocessor list and SOC 2 evidence, and 3) confirmation on how you plan to execute the agreement (DocuSign vs. AdobeSign preferred).

Specifics we need answered:
- Will Redwood provide the EU SCCs as an addendum or incorporate them into the DPA?
- For UK customers, do you use the IDTA addendum or a UK-specific clause set?
- Is there a named subprocessors file that we can include in the schedule?

We'd like to get a 2-week turnaround if possible; procurement is targeting July 26 to finish the contract phase.

Attaching nothing yet — procurement asked for your copy. Can you share the current redline and the subprocessor list?

Best,
Sofia

Thanks for the clear list. Attaching the current DPA with our running redlines (RI_DPA_Redlines_v3.docx) and our latest subprocessor export (Subprocessor_List_2027-07.csv). High level: we typically provide the EU SCCs as a standalone annex linked from the DPA (this keeps the doc compact) and we provide a UK IDTA addendum for UK deals. That said, if you prefer SCC language baked directly into the DPA we can accommodate that — legal will want to know which your counsel prefers.

Plan proposal:
- Marissa (legal) will review and propose negotiation positions on the redlines — cc'd.
- If substantive redlines remain, we can run a single DocuSign envelope that includes the DPA + SCC annex + subprocessor schedule, or execute the IDTA as a separate envelope for the UK.
- We aim to have a proposed final for Acme legal by July 20 to hit your July 26 target.

Let me know if procurement needs a PO/legal contact; happy to loop in our S&M lead.

Thanks,
Ben

Hi Sofia / Ben,

I reviewed RI_DPA_Redlines_v3.docx and pulled a short negotiation playbook. TL;DR: we recommend (1) accept SCCs as an annex + optional UK IDTA addendum, (2) narrow the transfer-impact language to avoid broad legal obligations that will slow signoff, and (3) provide a current subprocessor CSV as a schedule that can be updated with 30 days' notice.

Key redline points for Acme to expect (summary):
- Security & audit: we will share SOC 2 Type II summary and redacted report on an NDA basis; we do not provide full raw evidence by default.
- Transfer mechanism: SCC annex preferred; for UK we will attach the IDTA addendum. If Acme requires embedding SCC text in the DPA for its template, we can prepare that variant but it may add 2 business days to prep.
- Liability caps: suggest we keep them aligned with commercial deal terms — legal can confirm with procurement if they are requesting changes.
- Subprocessors: provide full list; for sensitive categories we recommend a prior notification + objection window rather than consent.

Attachments included: 
- RI_DPA_Redlines_v3.docx (redlines with comment bubbles)
- Subprocessor_List_2027-07.csv (export from vendor management)

Execution recommendation: single DocuSign envelope containing DPA + SCC annex + subprocessor schedule. For UK-only accounts we will include the IDTA addendum as an extra envelope if Acme legal prefers a separate signature flow.

Links: I've dropped the draft and playbook in the shared drive for your counsel: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cRIDPA-refs

Next steps: Ben / Kar could you confirm desired execution method (single envelope vs separate) and whether Acme counsel prefers SCC text embedded in the DPA or as an annex? We'll queue up the DocuSign envelope once we have that direction.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

This is helpful, thank you. Procurement confirms:

- Subprocessor schedule must list named subprocessors and indicate any that operate outside EU/UK.

Timeline: we still aim to sign by July 26. Please send the DocuSign envelope and SOC 2 summary when ready; I'll route to counsel and procurement immediately.

Thanks —
Sofia
